claims.natural_statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 046 (Shafarevich counterexamples in dimension two and with large fundamental group.; papers: A projective fourfold with large fundamental group and non-Stein universal cover; A surface counterexample to Shafarevich holomorphic convexity; Lean status: UNFORMALIZED (No Lean proof in openai/math)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.
Independent verification, with a dyadic multiplication-cover extension, of the actual surface-family infinite quotient and its based monodromy invariance.
Actual corrected monodromies preserve the five explicit mod-two characters and change each weight-two pair boundary in degree at least three.

The actual based covering group surjects onto the sphere group; equivariant core collapse gives the exact pinching square and transfers equalizers without assuming a monodromy-invariant pinching kernel.
Translation differences are a free basis and both translations and sign raise its weighted completed-algebra degree by one, including cyclic endpoints.
The acyclic leading involution differential selects half as many relations as generators; these impose the full pro-2 involution, not just its Frattini action.
Operator substitution into the regular translation action transfers F-Magnus lower bounds to the L component of the based collapse map.
At most 4^N parameter representatives per layer, with all covering-group basis equalities, impose invariance under the entire closed deep parameter subgroup.
A locally finite countable pro-2 relator presentation with convergent negative weighted Golod-Shafarevich expression is infinite.

A finite parameter cover has ramification index two at the distinguished degeneration; its meridians are killed, and finitely many other meridian powers can be added after compactification within the remaining weight budget.
The manuscript's Q is infinite, every punctured fiber has dense image, all boundary meridians have finite image, and distinguished-fiber meridians are trivial.
Finite detection of entire local boundary-group images lets the quotient map descend across normalization and all resolution meridians.
The distinguished reduced fiber on the final projective cover is a nodal union of smooth rational curves.
A connected component of the compact rational fiber has infinite image in the final surface group.

The surface manuscript's main theorem: a smooth projective surface contains a rational nodal curve of infinite fundamental-group image, producing a closed noncompact rational string in its universal cover and failure of holomorphic convexity.
Arithmetic orbifold geometry realizes the specified arrangements and a map from a blowup of a simple abelian surface.
Local model translation kernels are compatible and the projected-diameter graphs satisfy the required uniform hyperbolicity bounds.
The local path criterion detects a nontrivial translation after imposing true orbifold relations.
Comparison, cyclic upper bounds, and the surviving translation give an infinite cyclic image of the blown-up abelian surface in the orbifold group.
Projective ambient realization and repeated ambient blowdown embed a simple abelian surface with infinite cyclic fundamental-group image.
Interpolation, Bertini and Lefschetz turn the cyclic embedding into a large-group projective fourfold; the rank-three kernel obstructs a Stein universal cover.
The fourfold manuscript's main theorem: a large-group smooth projective fourfold has no positive-dimensional compact analytic subvarieties in its universal cover, which is nevertheless non-Stein.
The known linear Shafarevich theorem and the scope-qualified Eyssidieux-Funar theorem do not themselves decide the actual marked genus-zero quotient in this audit.
A locally finite countable pro-2 relator presentation with convergent negative weighted Golod-Shafarevich expression is infinite.

claims.natural_statement: For every n=2^r with r>=2, the actual paired elliptic sphere family defined by [n] admits the quotient construction of prop:infinite-quotient: at t=49/200 any J>=2n with (1+6n^2)t(4t)^J/(1-4t)<1/100 imposes all D_J monodromy equalities, and the involution relations plus any subsequently chosen finite boundary-power family of cost <1/100 leave an infinite pro-2 quotient with dense fiber image.

For a free discrete group on a regular (Z/n)^2 orbit, the iterated translation differences delta_T1^i delta_T2^j(a_00), 0<=i,j<n, form a discrete free basis by a triangular word substitution, hence also a free pro-2 basis.

For every dyadic n>=4 the actual joint marking/sign monodromy is (Z/n)^2 semidirect inversion C2, of order 2n^2; its mod-two group-algebra augmentation ideal has exact nilpotence index 2n, so D_(2n) kills this finite geometric action.

A compact connected nodal curve of smooth rational components with infinite fundamental-group image lifts to a closed noncompact rational string, on which every ambient holomorphic function is constant; its point hull is noncompact.
For a smooth projective variety, largeness of its fundamental group is equivalent to absence of positive-dimensional compact analytic subvarieties in its universal cover.

For every n=2^r with r>=2, the reviewed actual paired elliptic-family quotient yields a smooth connected projective complex surface X_n containing a connected nodal curve of smooth rational components with infinite fundamental-group image. Every connected lift of that curve to the universal cover is a closed noncompact locally finite rational string, and the holomorphic hull of each of its points is noncompact. The distinguished reduced fiber has the coset-incidence graph described by S_DUAL_GRAPH.

For arbitrary groups G,Q,P, a homomorphism rho:G->Q and p:Q->P injective on each subgroup A_i, if every element of S maps to a conjugate of an element of some A_i and is killed by p composed with rho, then the normal closure of S lies in ker(rho), and rho descends to G/normalClosure(S). Also ker(p composed with f)=ker(f) for every homomorphism f whose image lies in a detected A_i.

For a finite Galois cover with group P of the actual distinguished star fiber, trivial vertical monodromy, unmarked main P1, and k two-marked tails, let a_j be the first marked-point monodromy and C_j=<a_j>. The normalized fiber has main vertices P, tail vertices disjoint union P/C_j, and one edge (p,j) from p to p*C_j. If H=<a_j>, it has [P:H] components and total graph first Betti number |P|*(k-1)-sum_j |P|/|C_j|+[P:H]. This identifies the actual geometric fiber, not merely an abstract finite graph.

claims.natural_statement: For arbitrary groups G,Q,P, a homomorphism rho:G->Q and p:Q->P injective on each subgroup A_i, if every element of S maps to a conjugate of an element of some A_i and is killed by p composed with rho, then the normal closure of S lies in ker(rho), and rho descends to G/normalClosure(S). claims.formal_statement:
import Mathlib.GroupTheory.QuotientGroup.Basic

namespace SurfaceGeometry

universe u v w z

variable {G : Type u} {Q : Type v} {P : Type w} {I : Type z}
variable [Group G] [Group Q] [Group P]

theorem local_kernel_agreement
    (f : G →* Q) (p : Q →* P) (A : Subgroup Q)
    (himage : ∀ g, f g ∈ A)
    (hdetect : Set.InjOn p (A : Set Q)) :
    (p.comp f).ker = f.ker := by
  ext g
  change p (f g) = 1 ↔ f g = 1
  constructor
  · intro h
    exact hdetect (himage g) A.one_mem (by simpa using h)
  · intro h
    simp [h]

theorem conjugate_kernel_trivial
    (p : Q →* P) (A : Subgroup Q)
    (hdetect : Set.InjOn p (A : Set Q))
    {a : Q} (ha : a ∈ A) (g : Q)
    (h : p (g * a * g⁻¹) = 1) :
    g * a * g⁻¹ = 1 := by
  have hp : p a = 1 := by
    have h' := congrArg (fun t : P => (p g)⁻¹ * t * p g) h
    simpa [map_mul, map_inv, mul_assoc] using h'
  have haone : a = 1 :=
    hdetect ha A.one_mem (by simpa using hp)
  simp [haone]

theorem normal_closure_killed
    (rho : G →* Q) (p : Q →* P) (A : I → Subgroup Q)
    (S : Set G)
    (hdetect : ∀ i, Set.InjOn p (A i : Set Q))
    (hlocal : ∀ s ∈ S, ∃ i a g, a ∈ A i ∧ rho s = g * a * g⁻¹)
    (hfinite : ∀ s ∈ S, p (rho s) = 1) :
    Subgroup.normalClosure S ≤ rho.ker := by
  apply Subgroup.normalClosure_le_normal
  intro s hs
  change rho s = 1
  rcases hlocal s hs with ⟨i, a, g, ha, heq⟩
  rw [heq]
  apply conjugate_kernel_trivial p (A i) (hdetect i) ha g
  rw [← heq]
  exact hfinite s hs

theorem descent_exists
    (rho : G →* Q) (p : Q →* P) (A : I → Subgroup Q)
    (S : Set G)
    (hdetect : ∀ i, Set.InjOn p (A i : Set Q))
    (hlocal : ∀ s ∈ S, ∃ i a g, a ∈ A i ∧ rho s = g * a * g⁻¹)
    (hfinite : ∀ s ∈ S, p (rho s) = 1) :
    ∃ descended : G ⧸ Subgroup.normalClosure S →* Q,
      ∀ g, descended (QuotientGroup.mk g) = rho g := by
  have hker := normal_closure_killed rho p A S hdetect hlocal hfinite
  refine ⟨QuotientGroup.lift (Subgroup.normalClosure S) rho hker, ?_⟩
  intro g
  rfl

end SurfaceGeometry
